page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-8-lssd is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 8 vCPUs and 30 GB of system memory, providing 3.75 GB per core. The instance is powered by dedicated x86_64 Intel Xeon 6985P-C processors running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Its CPU features a 504 MB L3 cache alongside support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and hardware-accelerated cryptographic primitives like AES and SHA-NI. It includes a bundled 402 GB local NVMe SSD, but does not feature GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark measurements place the processor in the average tier across synthetic multi-core evaluations, yielding a Geekbench multi-core score of 7,017.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 15,406.43. Specialized tasks show distinct capabilities: Geekbench text processing reaches the top 10% (2,961.0), and single-threaded gzip compression performs in the top 25% at 36.27 GB/sec. Similarly, small-model (135M) LLM text generation performs in the top quartile at 277.66 tokens/sec. Conversely, memory subsystem performance exhibits tradeoffs: while cached small-block memory reads achieve 668.21 GB/sec, uncached large-block read bandwidth drops to 29.93 GB/sec, matching a PassMark memory score that falls in the bottom 25%.

Qualitatively, the c4-standard-8-lssd delivers a resource profile suited for compute tasks requiring high-speed local scratch disk space. While uncached memory throughput limits large, memory-bandwidth-bound analytics, the combination of hardware-assisted AMX extensions and integrated NVMe storage offers strong utility for low-latency operational workloads, web serving, text-heavy pipelines, small LLM inference, and mid-tier transactional databases.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-8-lssd is a general-purpose instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs (4 physical cores) on an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor clocked at 2.3 GHz, 30 GB of RAM, and a bundled 402 GB local NVMe SSD. It supports modern instruction sets including AVX-512, AMX, and cryptographic extensions, with no attached GPUs. Benchmarks demonstrate solid mid-tier general computing, highlighted by top-quartile results in text processing (Geekbench text score of 2,961.0), single-thread gzip compression (36.27 GB/sec), and small-model LLM text generation. While cached memory operations are swift, uncached large-block throughput ranks lower. The attached high-speed NVMe storage and balanced CPU-to-memory ratio make this server well suited for mid-tier databases, web serving, build systems, and localized text-processing pipelines.
